Kitchen Renovation Cost Per Square Foot UK

5 August 2026·BMB Renovation

Searching for the kitchen renovation cost per square foot can provide a useful starting point, but it is not a complete pricing method on its own. A small kitchen can cost more per square foot than a large one because fixed costs, such as design, plumbing changes, electrical work and installation, are spread over less floor area. In the UK, an estimate should combine the room’s size with the specification, the amount of labour involved and any structural changes. As a rough guide, a straightforward kitchen renovation might typically fall around £100 to £250 per square foot, while a high-specification project with bespoke cabinetry or major structural work can go considerably higher. Every project differs, particularly across Hertfordshire, North London and Bedfordshire, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

What does kitchen renovation cost per square foot include?

The first step is to decide what you mean by renovation. Replacing cabinet doors, worktops and appliances is very different from removing a wall, relocating the kitchen and renewing the plumbing and electrics. A per-square-foot figure may account for preparation and removal, cabinetry, worktops, appliances, flooring, tiling, plumbing, electrics, decorating and fitting. It may not include professional design fees, building control costs where applicable, structural calculations, waste removal or VAT, so check what each quotation covers before comparing prices. Measuring the floor area is simple: multiply the room’s length by its average width. However, use this only as a comparison tool rather than a promise of the final cost.

  • Cabinetry: this is often a substantial part of the overall budget. Flat-pack and entry-level modular units are usually cheaper, while rigid, painted or bespoke cabinets can cost more. Tall housing, corner mechanisms, pan drawers and internal storage can also increase the price.
  • Worktops: laminate is generally a lower-cost option. Solid timber, compact laminate, quartz and natural stone can add to the budget, especially where there are cut-outs for sinks, hobs and taps.
  • Appliances: allow for the fridge-freezer, oven, hob, extractor, dishwasher and washing machine if they are being replaced. Integrated appliances require careful cabinet planning and may cost more than freestanding equivalents.
  • Labour and fitting: this can include removal, cabinet installation, worktop fitting, plumbing, electrical work, tiling, flooring and finishing. The cost can rise when trades need to work around occupied rooms or when the layout changes.
  • Structural work: removing a wall, widening an opening, installing a steel beam, moving drainage or altering doors and windows can be a significant part of the budget. Structural work should be assessed separately rather than hidden inside a low per-square-foot figure.
  • Finishing work: painting, splashbacks, lighting, sockets, flooring, skirting and final adjustments are easy to overlook but can make a noticeable difference to the finished cost.

How the specification changes the price

A basic refresh may retain the existing layout, services and flooring. In that situation, the main costs are new doors or cabinets, a worktop, selected appliances and installation. A mid-range renovation may include new cabinets, a durable worktop, several integrated appliances, upgraded lighting, new flooring and a tiled splashback. A premium renovation could involve bespoke cabinetry, stone worktops, specialist finishes, a boiling-water tap, feature lighting and more complex joinery. These categories are useful for early budgeting, but they are not fixed UK price bands. The same kitchen size can produce very different quotes depending on product choices and site conditions.

Worked example: 80-square-foot kitchen refresh

Imagine a compact 8 ft by 10 ft kitchen, giving approximately 80 square feet of floor area. The homeowner keeps the sink, cooker position and existing flooring, but replaces the cabinets, worktop, sink, tap, extractor and a few appliances. As a rough guide, a project of this scope might typically have a budget of £8,000 to £14,000, equivalent to about £100 to £175 per square foot. The range allows for differences in cabinet quality, appliance brands, worktop material and the amount of preparation required. If the walls need repair, the electrics need updating or the floor is uneven, the final figure could be higher. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Worked example: 120-square-foot family kitchen

For a 10 ft by 12 ft room, the floor area is approximately 120 square feet. Suppose the plan includes new cabinets, a peninsula, laminate or compact worktops, five appliances, new flooring, a tiled splashback and additional sockets, while keeping the layout broadly similar. As a rough guide, an early allowance might typically be £15,000 to £25,000, or around £125 to £210 per square foot. Although the room is larger, the total is not simply 120 multiplied by a single rate: appliances, fitting and services are influenced by the number of units and connections rather than floor area alone. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

Worked example: 180-square-foot kitchen with structural work

Consider a 12 ft by 15 ft kitchen-diner, approximately 180 square feet, where a partition wall is removed, plumbing is relocated, electrics are extended and a new opening is formed. As a rough guide, with mid-to-high-range cabinetry, stone or engineered worktops, several appliances, flooring and decoration, a project of this type might typically have a budget of £30,000 to £50,000 or more. That equates to about £167 to £278 per square foot before unusually complex conditions are considered. The structural element may require design input, temporary works, a steel beam and additional finishing. Every project differs, so it is important to obtain a site-based assessment and a free, no-obligation quote rather than relying on a standard kitchen rate.

Labour, plumbing and electrical costs to check carefully

Installation quotations can differ because the word fitting covers different scopes. Ask whether the price includes removing and disposing of the old kitchen, levelling walls and floors, assembling cabinets, fitting worktops, connecting appliances, altering plumbing, installing sockets and lighting, tiling, flooring and decorating. Moving a sink or dishwasher may involve changes to hot, cold and waste pipes. A new induction hob or oven may need suitable electrical provision. If you are comparing companies, request a written schedule of work so you can see whether labour is included or shown separately. Ways to make a per-square-foot estimate more reliable

  • Measure both the floor area and the approximate length of the cabinet run. Cabinet quantity can affect the price more directly than room area.
  • List every appliance and state whether it is freestanding or integrated. Include extraction, refrigeration, laundry appliances and any specialist items.
  • Mark the current positions of the sink, waste, cooker, hob, radiators, doors and windows. Relocating these features can change labour and service costs.
  • Decide whether the quote should include flooring, tiling, lighting, decoration, waste removal and making good after structural work.
  • Keep a contingency for unknowns, such as damaged plaster, uneven floors, outdated wiring or concealed pipework. The appropriate allowance depends on the property and the project.
  • Ask for product specifications and installation assumptions, not just a single total. A low figure may exclude work that another contractor has included.

For homeowners in Watford and nearby areas, an accurate quotation normally starts with a survey of the existing kitchen and a conversation about the desired layout and specification. Frequently Asked Questions

What is the average kitchen renovation cost per square foot in the UK?+
As a rough guide, a straightforward renovation might typically cost about £100 to £250 per square foot. Premium finishes or structural work can take the figure higher. Every project is different, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
Is it cheaper to renovate a small kitchen?+
Not always. Small kitchens have less floor area over which to spread fixed costs such as design, preparation, fitting, plumbing and electrical work, so their cost per square foot can be higher.
Does kitchen renovation cost include appliances?+
It may or may not. Confirm whether the quotation includes appliances, delivery, installation and connection. Appliance choice and the number of units can significantly affect the total.
How much does moving a kitchen layout add to the cost?+
There is no single figure. Moving sinks, waste pipes, appliances, sockets or lighting can add labour and materials, while removing walls may also require structural design, a beam and making-good work.
How can I get an accurate kitchen renovation estimate?+
Arrange a site assessment and provide a clear list of cabinets, appliances, finishes and layout changes. Ask for an itemised quotation that states what labour, materials and finishing work are included.
